nodes.label: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
nodes.rationale: Critical examination of intrinsic self-correction (without external feedback) in LLMs; demonstrates performance degradation on reasoning tasks; identifies issues in prior work including oracle label reliance, unfair baseline comparisons, and suboptimal prompt design.

nodes.label: Intrinsic Self-Correction Concept
nodes.rationale: Self-correction without external feedback; model must independently determine correctness and decide whether to retain or revise answers; contrasts with oracle-guided approaches that use ground-truth labels.

nodes.label: Self-Correction Performance Findings
nodes.rationale: Intrinsic self-correction decreases accuracy across GSM8K, CommonSenseQA, HotpotQA; models more likely to convert correct answers to incorrect ones; GPT-4/4-Turbo retain initial answers more often due to higher confidence.

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Debate vs Self-Consistency
nodes.rationale: Multi-agent debate underperforms self-consistency with equivalent number of responses; improvement attributed to consistency voting rather than genuine self-correction or debate mechanism.

nodes.label: Prompt Design Issues in Self-Correction
nodes.rationale: Improvements in prior work stem from suboptimal initial prompts; feedback prompts contain task specifications absent from initial prompts; integrating feedback into initial prompt yields better results than self-correction.

nodes.label: Oracle Label Dependency in Self-Correction
nodes.rationale: Prior work (RCI, Reflexion) uses ground-truth labels to determine when to stop self-correction; improvements vanish without oracle feedback; counter-intuitive for reasoning tasks where ground truth availability negates need for LLM problem-solving.

nodes.label: Inference Cost Parity in Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Self-correction uses multiple LLM responses; fair comparison requires baselines with equivalent inference costs; multi-agent debate should be compared against self-consistency with same number of responses.
